ST0001's criterion ids make intent doctor exit 1, and that blocks ST0001/01's gate install. Doctor reports 4 model-inconsistent findings: AC-04 belongs to WP-04, which ST0001 does not have, and likewise AC-05, AC-06 and AC-07. Intent reads a criterion id as AC-<gg>.<n>, where gg is the work package seq, or 00 for a thread-level criterion (group_seq and the 'belongs to WP' check in native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/doctor.rs; withdrawn and descoped criteria are exempt, and so is group 00). So WP02's AC-04 and AC-05 read as WP-04 and WP-05, WP03's AC-06 as WP-06, and the thread-level AC-07 as WP-07. AC-01 to AC-03 pass only by coincidence: AC-02 and AC-03 are WP01's but read as WP02's and WP03's. They are your criteria, so I have not touched them. A CLI-only fix: withdraw AC-04 to AC-07 with a reason and recreate them as AC-02.1, AC-02.2, AC-03.1 and AC-00.1, re-satisfying the two WP02 rows with their evidence; for honest grouping, do the same for AC-01 to AC-03 as AC-01.1 to AC-01.3. While doctor exits 1, intent claude upgrade --apply would install a pre-commit gate that refuses every commit, yours included, so I am holding --apply and doing the rest of ST0001/01 now: languages declared (rust, shell), then agents sync, README's stale Intent line and the first backup. Tell me when doctor is clean and I will announce, then apply. The report-only run shows apply writes .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md, usage-rules.md, .intent_critic.yml and the pre-commit, post-merge, post-checkout and post-rewrite hooks; no existing hook is overwritten.

ISSUE:0002 red, before the fix: d6408f1 adds renewal_write_keeps_claude_items_readable_by_security (ignored; CI still runs the old test). Reproduce: cargo test --locked --lib renewal_write_keeps_claude_items_readable_by_security -- --ignored. Output on rhadamanth: panicked at src/auth.rs:1012:5, 'partitions after the renewal write: ["cdhash:9dbfbfa21ae33cd8278abc0e0757b53168ec83a7"]'. Before that write the item's partitions were apple-tool: plus the test binary's own cdhash; ccusage's in-process write reset them to the writer's partition alone, so it fails on the partition assertion, not on access. Log: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Ccusage/e1e5d4f2-40c1-4c02-8b5f-93719b6fc69d/scratchpad/issue-0002/red.log. Research findings (Claude Code 2.1.317 binary, read-only, and experiments on disposable keychains). (1) Service: 'Claude Code' + OAUTH_FILE_SUFFIX + '-credentials' + '-' + the first 8 hex of sha256 over NFC(CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR) when set, else over NFC(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as given, unresolved); account: $USER, else os.userInfo().username, and claude-code-user when the name has a character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-]; stdin limit: the whole security -i line, newline included, at most 4032 characters (security itself splits lines near 4096); exit 44 is errSecItemNotFound and 36 errSecInteractionNotAllowed; 2 s timeout per call. (2) A keychain created outside ~/Library/Keychains is version 256 with no partition list at all, so the fixture keychain lives in ~/Library/Keychains as ccusage-test-<pid>-<n>.keychain-db; create-keychain leaves the search list alone and the fixture is deleted on drop. (3) A write through security -i also resets the partitions to its writer's, apple-tool:, which is why writing through security keeps the items readable. (4) find-generic-password -w prints the password as hex when any byte is non-printing, eg a non-ASCII character in the JSON, so the reader decodes both. (5) security's stderr echoes the hex of a line it cannot parse, so ccusage never shows security's output. (6) There is no security command to add an app to an existing item's decrypt ACL, and the write path needs only the partition (the encrypt entry allows any app), so the test grants the partition alone. (7) Safety incident, contained: security -i add-generic-password with a keychain path that does not exist silently adds to the default keychain. My first experiment did that, putting one fake item (service ccusage-exp-51447, account fixture-user, one 0x00 byte) into hv's login keychain at 09:17Z by its own creation date. I deleted that exact item at once (lookup now exits 44). No real item was read or changed, and find-generic-password does not fall back. Every write since checks that its keychain file exists, and the fix's update-only lookup refuses before any write to a keychain that is not there. Next, the fix: /usr/bin/security for read and write, NFC service names (unicode-normalization, macOS only), and security-framework only as a macOS dev-dependency for the test. I carry on unless you say wait.

ISSUE:0002 ready for validation: red at d6408f1, fix at 812264d. Reproduce: git checkout d6408f1 && cargo test --locked --lib renewal_write_keeps_claude_items_readable_by_security -- --ignored (red on the partition assertion), then at 812264d the same command passes (green.log beside red.log in my scratchpad). Also at 812264d: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked (33 unit, 21 CLI, 1 ignored), cargo build --release --locked, sh tests/release.sh (20 scenarios), actionlint and intent critic rust all pass. What changed: src/keychain.rs (macOS only) reads with find-generic-password -a <account> -w -s <service>, decoding the hex form security prints for non-printing bytes, and writes with security -i, sending add-generic-password -U -a ... -s ... -X <hex> <keychain> on stdin; security's output is discarded. Update-only: a metadata find (no -w) locates the item and its keychain first, and the write targets that keychain, because -U adds a missing item and security falls back to the default keychain when the named one does not exist; the item is read back after the write. The 4032-character stdin limit is checked in prepare_write, before the token exchange, and again at the write; nothing ever falls back to argv (Acceptance 3: writer() has the single argument -i, pinned by a unit test). Account: $USER, else id -un, else claude-code-user, as Claude Code does. service() hashes the NFC form of the config dir (unicode-normalization, macOS only), with a unit test for both spellings of é. Locks unchanged. CI's macOS step now runs the new test; the old test is gone. security-framework is a macOS dev-dependency for the test alone, and the release binary no longer links Security.framework (otool -L). README's two Keychain paragraphs and docs/releasing.md are rewritten. Notes for you and hv: (1) tools/test-keychain-upgrade, tests/keychain-upgrade.swift and docs/releasing.md's paragraph on them check that signed builds keep in-process Keychain trust, which ccusage no longer uses; I left them for hv to rule on removing. (2) Linux was not compiled here (only the macOS std is installed); every Keychain path is cfg macOS, and CI's Linux jobs will show it. (3) The pre-exchange size check sees the current document; a renewal that grew a document across the limit would fail after the exchange, but growth is bounded by refreshTokenExpiresAt and token length. (4) The post-release check on hv's accounts waits for your verdict and hv's OK. (5) WP03's ARCHITECTURE and RULES notes can now be written from this.

ISSUE:0002 handover (09:34Z), note (2) update: Linux now clippy-checks clean on rhadamanth. At 812264d's code (src, tests, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are unchanged since), cargo clippy --all-targets --locked --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -D warnings exits 0 with no warnings, covering the lib, the bin and the cli test. It is a check only, with no link and no test run: std was built from rust-src with -Zbuild-std (RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1, Homebrew Rust 1.99.1), and ring's C with Homebrew LLVM clang under ring's own sysroot-free flags, -nostdlibinc -DRING_CORE_NOSTDLIBINC=1. x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu cannot be checked that way: ring's x86-64 C reaches stdlib.h through immintrin.h, which is why ring's build script leaves x86-64 out of that path. ccusage has no target_arch, target_env or pointer-width cfg, only target_os = "macos" and unix, so the ARM64 check covers the same cfg surface. CI's four jobs stay the full proof. Log: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Ccusage/e1e5d4f2-40c1-4c02-8b5f-93719b6fc69d/scratchpad/linux-check/clippy-aarch64-linux.log

ISSUE:0002: both probe items are deleted from login.keychain-db. Before deleting, a metadata-only scan (security dump-keychain without -d, printing only records whose acct is fixture-user or ccusage-fixture, or whose svce is len<n>, ccusage-exp-<n>, svc-a or ccusage-test-*) found exactly two of the 217 records: svce len4100 and len8000, acct fixture-user, cdat and mdat 20261103091748Z. They came from experiment.zsh's line-length loop (3900, 4100 and 8000 hex digits); len3900 fit, went to the disposable keychain and was deleted with it. I deleted each with security delete-generic-password -a fixture-user -s <svc> naming login.keychain-db (both exit 0). Lookups by the same attributes now exit 44, the scan counts 215 records and 0 fixture matches. experiment2.zsh and experiment3.zsh only sent short lines to keychain files they had checked exist, so nothing else could have fallen back. Your two notes: I am taking both as one small follow-up commit, which I will hand to you. (a) update() reads back from the keychain locate() found. (b) The test comment says update()'s own -w read-back would prompt first, and docs/releasing.md says to deny a dialog during that test. My watch-out 1 now names the second fallback: a security -i line over 4097 bytes, newline included, loses its keychain argument.
